# Tibbles {.unnumbered}

All *tidyverse* packages use an special type of data structure called **tibble**, that is the next evolution of the data frames at R. 

**Tibbles** are similar to data frames but they have special features that make them more interesting for data analysis. 

**Remember!!** First all we need to load *tidyverse* package (take into account that this package will load all tidyverse packages including tibble one).






::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(tidyverse)
```
:::







## Data Frames vs Tibbles

### Printing

This is how `iris` data set looks as a data frame object:






::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
head(iris)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
  Sepal.Length Sepal.Width Petal.Length Petal.Width Species
1          5.1         3.5          1.4         0.2  setosa
2          4.9         3.0          1.4         0.2  setosa
3          4.7         3.2          1.3         0.2  setosa
4          4.6         3.1          1.5         0.2  setosa
5          5.0         3.6          1.4         0.2  setosa
6          5.4         3.9          1.7         0.4  setosa
```


:::
:::






Now we are going to convert `iris` to a tibble, we will use tidyverse function `as_tibble()`:






::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
iris_tb <- as_tibble(iris)
head(iris_tb)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
# A tibble: 6 x 5
  Sepal.Length Sepal.Width Petal.Length Petal.Width Species
         <dbl>       <dbl>        <dbl>       <dbl> <fct>  
1          5.1         3.5          1.4         0.2 setosa 
2          4.9         3            1.4         0.2 setosa 
3          4.7         3.2          1.3         0.2 setosa 
4          4.6         3.1          1.5         0.2 setosa 
5          5           3.6          1.4         0.2 setosa 
6          5.4         3.9          1.7         0.4 setosa 
```


:::
:::






We see that in the console...
* output of the data frame we only get the data displayed directly and unorganized.
* output of the tibble shows a summary of dimensions as well as a compact visualization of the columns and types of each column. 

### Column Names

On tibbles column names don't need to be consecutive you can have names with spaces, like this example:






::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
dt <- tibble(
  p  = c("A", "B", "C", "D", "E"),
  x = 1:5,
  y = 2,
  `sum of values` = x + y # we can reference other columns
)
dt
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
# A tibble: 5 x 4
  p         x     y `sum of values`
  <chr> <int> <dbl>           <dbl>
1 A         1     2               3
2 B         2     2               4
3 C         3     2               5
4 D         4     2               6
5 E         5     2               7
```


:::
:::






### Selection

When selecting and modifying values you can work the same as a data frame but consider that the output of any selection will return a data frame always...






::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# first value of first column as DF
dt[1,1]
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
# A tibble: 1 x 1
  p    
  <chr>
1 A    
```


:::
:::






If we want to manipulate the value we will need to do a second selection






::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# first value of first column
dt[1,1][[1]]
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] "A"
```


:::
:::







You need to use name selection or double selection to access the values itself.






::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# first column as vector
dt$p
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] "A" "B" "C" "D" "E"
```


:::
:::

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# first column value as value
dt[[1]][1]
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] "A"
```


:::
:::






## Creating a tibble

In case you need to create a tibble manually, you can defined it as the following example.






::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
dt <- tibble(
  p  = c("A", "B", "C", "D", "E"),
  x = 1:5,
  y = 2,
  `sum of values` = x + y
)
dt
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
# A tibble: 5 x 4
  p         x     y `sum of values`
  <chr> <int> <dbl>           <dbl>
1 A         1     2               3
2 B         2     2               4
3 C         3     2               5
4 D         4     2               6
5 E         5     2               7
```


:::
:::
